rules.entry: Explicitly confirmed current repeatable weekly running seconds and continuous running seconds are required in every context. Beginner means short demonstrated run intervals, not absent evidence. A returning runner must supply newly demonstrated capacity after the break. Historical performance is excluded.
rules.frequency: Runner explicitly selects 2 or 3 sessions within actual availability; never infer desired frequency from available weekdays.
rules.workload: Distribute current weekly running seconds equally, placing remainder seconds in earlier slots. Add the authored per-session seconds for each stage. Week 4 returns to initial running load. These are original review candidates, not validated progression limits.
rules.structure: Currently training uses continuous easy running bounded by confirmed continuous capacity. Beginner and non-health return use consecutive running intervals each no longer than confirmed continuous capacity, separated by 60-second walks. No walking recovery after the last running interval. Warm-up and cooldown are walking.
rules.advancement: All future stages are conditional research illustrations. Advancement requires fresh performance and health reassessment. No automatic advancement is authorized.
rules.transition: After week 4, reassess current capacity against the exact goal-specific policy. Completing scheduled weeks alone never establishes readiness.
rules.health: Health-related interruptions, pain and illness require review. Break length does not prescribe a reduction.
rules.higher_frequency: Four or more workouts require another authored policy; extra available days are scheduling alternatives.

limitations: All numbers are original candidate values requiring qualified review
Added running and walking loads are unreviewed
No automatic advancement or goal transition
